quickCards.title: Heat Wave Cool-Room Loop
quickCards.summary: Cycle shade, airflow, hydration, and room checks before the house gets dangerous.
quickCards.bodyMarkdown:
## First 10 Minutes
- Close blinds on sun-facing windows.
- Stage water, medications, and chargers in one cool room.

## Keep Doing
- Rotate people and pets through the cool room.
- Limit oven, dryer, and heavy appliance use until evening.

## Leave Early If
- Indoor heat keeps climbing.
- Anyone becomes confused, stops sweating, or cannot cool down.

## Do Not
- Trap everyone in the hottest room.
- Wait until the house feels dangerous before planning transport.

quickCards.title: Wildfire Smoke Clean-Room Setup
quickCards.summary: Build one lower-smoke room quickly and keep it clean enough to rest in.
quickCards.bodyMarkdown:
## Seal
- Shut windows and exterior doors.
- Block obvious drafts with materials you can remove fast.

## Filter
- Run the best filter setup you already know how to use.
- Keep doors closed once the room is staged.

## Protect
- Leave smoky jackets, shoes, and cleanup tools outside the room.
- Keep medications, water, and chargers inside.

## Move If Needed
- Indoor air keeps worsening.
- Anyone struggles to breathe or cannot recover after getting inside.

quickCards.title: Flood Water Entry Stop-Check
quickCards.summary: Use a stop-check-move sequence when water is rising or entering the home.
quickCards.bodyMarkdown:
## Stop
- Pause before troubleshooting.
- Check footing, exits, and who still needs to move.

## Check
- Note where water is entering and what outlets or appliances are nearby.
- Lift documents, lights, and medications above the expected water line.

## Move
- Shift go-bags, chargers, and dry layers toward the safest exit.
- Leave before stairs, doors, or roads are cut off.

## Do Not
- Keep wading once you lose dry footing.
- Reset gear while water and electricity risks are still unclear.
